discussion_comments.comment_body: These now end up as exported symbols: on Linux we link `python` with `-Xlinker -export-dynamic` (and libpython is a shared object with `--enable-shared`), so we are exporting around 140 `_PyPegen_*_rule` functions. Worse, any pegen-generated extension with the same rule names (e.g. `make build` in `Tools/peg_generator` after modifying `python.gram`) defines the very same `_PyPegen_expression_rule` & co, and the calls between `parse.c` and `parse_invalid.c` can be interposed by the interpreter's copies, so you silently run CPython's rule instead of the one you just generated. This also means that in non-PGO shared builds hot rules like `expression_rule` go through the PLT. Can we mark the shared declarations/definitions with `Py_LOCAL_SYMBOL` so they stay internal?
